clue.text: March direct into second-grade territory

indicators.note: the word for direct is placed into the letters made from second-grade territory

parts.note: B is a second grade, after A
land is territory
to direct is to order

explanation.surface: An instruction to march troops into some second-rate territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like a verb or the month; here it is the noun for a frontier region.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is a frontier district, the strip of country along a boundary.

clue.text: Crumbs of comfort for them are trivial

definitions.text: Crumbs of comfort for them are trivial

parts.words: Crumbs of comfort for them are trivial
parts.note: breadcrumbs are scattered for these creatures, and anything trivial is said to be for them

explanation.definitionFit: Something worthless is called 'for the birds', and crumbs are left out to feed them.

clue.text: Jewel-thieves' contact at the barrier

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery
a fence receives stolen goods from thieves

explanation.surface: Jewel thieves meeting their middleman at the fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-fence is an enclosing fence, figuratively a protective barrier around funds.

clue.text: All-rounder shows promise before the match

definitions.text: All-rounder shows promise before the match

parts.words: All-rounder shows promise before the match
parts.note: not a cricketer showing early form but a circular token signifying a pledge before a wedding

explanation.definitionFit: A band given when a couple pledge to marry, made before the wedding.

clue.text: A stretch at the Yard?

parts.note: Scotland Yard is the London police HQ; the reach of the law is described as a lengthy limb, and a stretch is also a prison term

explanation.definitionFit: The long arm of the law is the far-reaching power of the police.

clue.text: New domain many such tribes seek

definitions.text: New domain many such tribes seek

indicators.note: new here means the letters of domain made new in another order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many

explanation.surface: Wandering peoples forever in search of fresh territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal, not part of the picture. The whole clue also describes wandering peoples, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering tribes move from place to place looking for new pastures.

clue.text: Female 1 dn writers

explanation.surface: Female birds who take up writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 dn is BIRDS: a female swan is called a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A female swan is a pen, and pens are instruments people write with.

clue.text: Material returned by this poet

indicators.note: returned means the word for the material is read backwards

parts.note: toile is a fabric, a material

explanation.surface: A poet sending back some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot (or George Eliot) is a celebrated writer of verse.

clue.text: Old theologian, one of twenty-two in Harrow's song

definitions.text: Old theologian, one of twenty-two in Harrow's song

parts.words: Old theologian, one of twenty-two in Harrow's song
parts.note: medieval scholastic theologians, and the school's men: the 'twenty-two' of the Harrow school song Forty Years On are the players of Harrow football

explanation.definitionFit: Medieval scholastic philosophers were called by this name; the Harrow players are literally men of the school.

clue.text: All that Barmecide's guest had to chew over?

definitions.text: All that Barmecide's guest had to chew over?

parts.words: All that Barmecide's guest had to chew over?
parts.note: in the Arabian Nights the Barmecide served a beggar an imaginary feast, so the guest had only ideas to eat

explanation.definitionFit: Something worth thinking about is mental nourishment, the only kind the Barmecide's guest got.

clue.text: We see German physicist get on badly in the Navy

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the abbreviation for the navy

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of get on come out in disorder

explanation.surface: A German scientist struggles to get along in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' signals the anagram and 'in' puts it inside the navy abbreviation. 'We see' nods to the X-rays he discovered, which let us see inside the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Röntgen was the German physicist who discovered X-rays.

clue.text: Like Othello's doctor or his replacement

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: a replacement here is a rearrangement of the letters of his

explanation.surface: Asking whether Othello's physician or a stand-in should treat him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges HIS into ISH. Othello was a Moor, so something like his is of that people.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the Moor of Venice, so his traits are those of the Moors.

clue.text: Chest-protector?

parts.note: not a piece of armour for the torso but something protecting a strongbox of valuables

explanation.definitionFit: A safe is a strong chest, and a guard protects it; generally the word means a protection.

clue.text: The same again for one abstainer in the party

indicators.note: the pieces for one and abstainer are placed inside the word for party

parts.note: a do is a party
I is the Roman numeral one
TT means teetotal, a drinks abstainer

explanation.surface: A lone teetotaller at a party orders the same once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is the word used to repeat what was just said, meaning likewise.

clue.text: The point en——'d too! Then, ——, to thy work" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: The point en——'d too! Then, ——, to thy work" (Hamlet)

parts.words: The point en——'d too! Then, ——, to thy work" (Hamlet)
parts.note: Hamlet's line on finding the poisoned rapier tip: the same word fills both gaps, once after en-

explanation.definitionFit: In Hamlet, the poisoned sword tip is called envenomed, and the poison itself is told to do its work.

clue.text: Growth of the Middle Kingdom

parts.note: not China but plant life, the kingdom placed between animal and mineral

explanation.definitionFit: Plant life forms the kingdom between animal and mineral in the old three-way division.

clue.text: One mad frolic in small measure to enlarge upon?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are put inside the abbreviation for a small measure

parts.note: mm is a millimetre, a small measure
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: mad suggests these letters are wildly disordered

explanation.surface: A single crazy prank blown out of all proportion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges I plus FROLIC into ICROFIL, placed 'in' MM. 'enlarge upon' is literal: tiny film images are blown up to be read.
explanation.definitionFit: Microfilm holds documents photographed very small, which a reader magnifies to view.

clue.text: Elephant-hunter's dreams of such a portal are delusive

definitions.text: Elephant-hunter's dreams of such a portal are delusive

parts.words: Elephant-hunter's dreams of such a portal are delusive
parts.note: an elephant-hunter wants tusks; in Homer false dreams come through a gate made of tusk material, true ones through horn

explanation.definitionFit: In Homer and Virgil deceptive dreams pass through the gate made of tusk, true ones through horn.

clue.text: Suburban country, (not for a Judo beginner)

explanation.surface: Edge-of-town fields are no place for a judo novice.
explanation.definitionFit: The protected countryside around a town is its green belt; in judo, a green belt grade is above a beginner's white.

clue.text: Former devout Russian breathed his last

parts.note: ex means former
pi is short for pious, devout
a Red is a Russian communist

explanation.surface: A one-time pious Russian dies.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire is to die, giving out one's final breath.

clue.text: Eccentric author, 'e lived by a pond

indicators.note: eccentric hints at the letters of author and e being jumbled up

parts.note: the dropped-aitch 'e gives the letter E

explanation.surface: An odd writer, in cockney speech, who lived beside a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' rearranges AUTHOR plus E. The American writer lived two years in a cabin beside Walden Pond.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Walden spent two years living in a hut beside a pond in Massachusetts.

clue.text: Spine-penetrating north wind?

indicators.note: wind as a verb, to twist, so the letters of north are turned about

explanation.surface: A north wind so bitter it cuts to the backbone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' reads as the noun for weather, but it is the verb, to twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spine on a plant stem.

clue.text: Canal horse pulls in London's tourists

explanation.surface: A barge horse drawing crowds of London sightseers.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse towing a barge is one who tows; the Tower of London is a big attraction for visitors.

clue.text: Makes keen, injecting, party faint-hearts with aspiration

indicators.note: injecting the faint-hearts with something puts it inside them

parts.note: wets were the timid moderates in the Conservative party
H is the aspirate, the breathed letter

explanation.surface: Getting timid party members fired up with ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition; it is the breathed sound H.
explanation.definitionFit: To whet a blade or an appetite is to sharpen it.

clue.text: Model is one paid to do office work

parts.note: a pro is a professional, someone paid for their work
taken as written
to type is a typical office task

explanation.surface: A fashion model who takes a salaried secretarial job.
explanation.definitionFit: A prototype is the first example on which later versions are based.

clue.text: Always the first of them to turn out

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: the first of picks the opening letter of them

explanation.surface: Always the first of them to turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: To evert something is to turn it inside out.

clue.text: Pass Italians need to get into Austria

definitions.text: Italians need to get into Austria

explanation.surface: A route Italians must cross to reach Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brenner is the Alpine mountain pass between Italy and Austria.

clue.text: Avenger out to impress

indicators.note: out means the letters of avenger are put out of order

explanation.surface: A revenge-seeker determined to make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to cut a design into a surface, impressing it there.

clue.text: How it is taken with no trouble at all

explanation.surface: Describing how something is received, effortlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: One is told to take it easy, meaning to relax; easily done means without difficulty.

clue.text: Average job in marine insurance

parts.note: in marine insurance, average is the sharing of a loss, and working out each party's share is a specific task

explanation.definitionFit: Average adjustment is the calculation apportioning a marine loss among the parties.
